decision: The user chooses who writes code. Nobody else edits files.
Sign-in opens Chrome only. The user never sees a terminal or an installer.
why: A person clicking Sign in does not have a command-line tool and should not be shown one.

decision: The desktop app is Home, Chat, Integrations, and a user panel. Home stays empty. Chat is stored with the project.
why: The notch stays the quick bar. The window is where the person reads the chat and connects models.

decision: The desktop app can read the project folder. Only the assigned writer can change files.
why: Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok need the same file access as their own apps, without a trust prompt or a broken tools flag.

decision: The project keeps a Graphify knowledge graph in graphify-out. After work that changes files, agents run graphify update .
why: Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, and Grok can read one current map of the project instead of starting from raw files.

decision: The person chooses the folder the models can read. The shared memory stays in this project. Only the assigned writer can change files in that folder.
why: Cursor and Claude let you point them at a folder. This app needs the same choice.

decision: Each folder keeps its own chats. Switching folders switches the conversation, the way a workspace does.
why: A chat from one folder was still showing after another folder was chosen.

decision: The notch closes when the pointer leaves it.
why: Sending a message or leaving the cursor in the top of the screen was keeping the panel open.

decision: The notch chat scrolls through the whole thread.
why: The panel was jumping back to the latest line on every frame, so earlier replies could not be read.

decision: Each folder keeps its own brain. The goal, decisions, handoffs, chats, writer and mode for a folder live in that folder's .brain. The app's own .brain keeps only app settings: the open folder and which models are switched on.
why: Models working on another folder were being briefed with Project Brain's own build history. This replaces the earlier decision that the shared memory stays in this project.

decision: The code writer works between two Undo snapshots kept in .brain/checkpoints, a hidden Git history separate from the folder's own .git. Only the newest change can be undone, and Undo refuses to wipe later edits unless the person confirms.
why: The writer edits files without asking, so people need a safe way back.

decision: Team memory is shared through the folder's own Git repo. Shared: manifest, goal, now, summary, decisions, handoffs. Personal (gitignored in .brain/.gitignore): local.json with the writer, mode and last-change time, chats, Undo history, the last debate, usage, config.
why: The person chose Git over a server. Writer and mode are personal choices, and decisions.jsonl/handoffs.jsonl use union merge so teammates' lines both survive.
